source_refs.note: Our Star (SUN): a main subheading of 13.6 Stellar Evolution, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 14-17.

blocks.text: The Sun is the nearest star to Earth and the main source of heat and light for our planet. It was formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a huge cloud of gas and dust called a solar nebula. Due to gravitational contraction, the temperature at the centre increased and a protostar was formed. When the core became extremely hot, nuclear fusion started in which hydrogen changed into helium and released a large amount of energy. The life stages of the Sun are: nebula, protostar, main sequence, red giant, planetary nebula, and white dwarf. At present, the Sun is in the main sequence stage, where it is producing heat and light by converting hydrogen into helium. In thermal physics, the Sun is important because it is a natural source of enormous heat energy and transfers this energy mainly by radiation.

blocks.alt: On a black panel titled Life Cycle of the Sun, a timeline marked Birth and then 1 to 14, in billions of years (approx.). The Sun grows slowly from birth through gradual warming; an arrow marks Now between 4 and 5. It becomes a red giant at about 10, a planetary nebula at about 11 and a white dwarf from about 12 to 14. Sizes not drawn to scale.

blocks.text: A star has mass 2 × 10³⁰ kg and radius 7 × 10⁸ m. Calculate gravitational pressure and compare it with internal pressure 1.0 × 10¹⁴ Pa.
Pg = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²)(2 × 10³⁰ kg)²/(7 × 10⁸ m)⁴
As both pressures are nearly equal, therefore, the star is in stable equilibrium.
book_errors: the star is in stable equilibrium

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Example 13.3: 6.67 × 4 × 10⁴⁹/2.401 × 10³⁵ = 2.668 × 10⁵⁰/2.401 × 10³⁵ ≈ 1.1 × 10¹⁵ Pa, not 1.3 × 10¹⁴ Pa. This is about eleven times the internal pressure of 1.0 × 10¹⁴ Pa, so the pressures are not equal and the star is not in equilibrium: gravity wins and the star contracts.

blocks.title: For your information
blocks.text: A neutron star is so dense that one teaspoon of its material would have a mass over 5.5 × 10¹² kg, about 900 times the mass of the Great Pyramid of Giza. The entire mass of the Earth at neutron star density would fit into a sphere 305 m in diameter.
A massive star has mass 4 × 10³⁰ kg, radius 5 × 10⁸ m and internal pressure 1 × 10¹⁴ Pa. Check whether the star is stable.
Gravity is stronger, therefore, the star will contract and may eventually collapse (possible neutron star or black hole formation).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Example 13.4: 6.67 × 16 × 10⁴⁹/6.25 × 10³⁴ ≈ 1.7 × 10¹⁶ Pa, not 1.7 × 10¹⁵ Pa. The conclusion (gravity is stronger and the star contracts) is unchanged.
A star has mass 1 × 10³⁰ kg, radius 1 × 10⁹ m and internal pressure 5 × 10¹⁴ Pa. Determine the state of the star.
Internal pressure dominates, therefore, the star will expand and may evolve into a red giant.
